correspondence.component_scope: Selected small wetland/pond opening south of Kgun Lake
correspondence.finding: The opening enlargement shows small ponds, marsh symbols and fine branching channels in the chosen initial setting. It does not continuously establish the complete selected westward opening and subsequent northward transfer into the larger southern lake-approach channel. Nearby water and the supplied modeled joins do not establish that missing through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern channel approach into the elongated Kgun Lake arm
correspondence.finding: The readable opening map shows the larger northward channel network entering the elongated southern lake arm. The selected approach and its lake entrance are geographically accounted for at ordinary corridor scale. The small approach channel has no independently established hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Elongated southern arm and southwestern Kgun Lake passage
correspondence.finding: Overlapping opening, northern and overview originals show the connected open-water arms, intervening lake neck and southwestern side of Kgun Lake. The selected long northward arm and westward turn occupy this lake passage. Kgun Lake is directly labeled on the original cartography; it is a lake component and is not assigned as a river-group name. No exact shoreline registration is required.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected northwestern lake, pond and wetland transfer toward the Manokinak corridor
correspondence.finding: The northern original depicts a Kgun-side channel, several separate lakes and ponds, small branching streams and a separately labeled Manokinak River farther west. The complete selected northward loop, southwestward lake-chain traverse and westward transfer are not established as a connected water route by the source. Individual mapped water bodies and an eventual receiving river do not resolve those intervening through-links.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward network traverse and selected detour north of Nuskealik Lake
correspondence.finding: The western original maps the Nungatak and Manokinak river network, intervening lakes and marshes, and Nuskealik Lake to the south. The selected westward traverse and southwestward detour through the lakes before its eastward return are not continuously established as the chosen water route. A clearly mapped Manokinak course lies in this network, but its name cannot be extended across the unresolved selected lake/wetland connections.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected Manokinak River corridor beside Nuskealik Lake and broad downstream reach
correspondence.finding: The western and lower originals overlap across the eastward return and show the selected connected river corridor east of Nuskealik Lake, the broad water reach below it, the southwestward turn near Iwaktok Hill and the subsequent large bends. Repeated Manokinak River labels support this component. The lake beside the river is not silently substituted for a demonstrated through-lake passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Mapped Manokinak–Azun branch junction
correspondence.finding: The lower original shows the southern branch leaving the westward Manokinak corridor, with Azun River labels along the selected southern branch. The branch junction and the selected transfer into it are geographically established. This is evidence for connected distinct named components, not a requirement that both have one name.

correspondence.component_scope: Azun River large bends and eastern tributary junction
correspondence.finding: The lower and terminal originals show the selected continuous Azun River channel through its large bends and the eastern tributary connection labeled Talik River. The source distinguishes neighboring Anerkochik and other wetland channels from the selected river. All stored joins in this lower interval are accounted for at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Final Azun bend and actual selected terminal in the widened lower channel
correspondence.finding: The terminal original covers the final large bend, the final selected part and the widened Azun River channel containing both supplied endpoint positions. The selected tip is geographically accounted for in that lower river setting, upstream of the outer coast shown by the wider regional context. The model sea class is not independent evidence that this tip is a surveyed river mouth; the selection is not extended to a different coastal ending.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwest opening and northward Claro reach
correspondence.finding: The selected opening matches the southern start of the mapped upper Claro corridor, continuing north to its pronounced eastward bend. The field-study sector map distinguishes it from adjacent headward tributaries.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward upper river and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: Study Maps 1–2 continue the same Claro across the eastward reach and its intervening tributary junctions.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeast-trending middle Claro
correspondence.finding: The mapped river continues southeast through the study’s canyon and lower-valley sectors. Its floodplain includes peatland, meadow and wooded settings.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Claro, Indio junction and Fagnano inlet
correspondence.finding: Maps 1–4 distinguish the eastern Indio input from the selected Claro. The lower Claro then enters Fagnano/Khami’s north shore through the mapped low wetland corridor. Yehuin, Chepelmuth and Yakush belong to the separate tributary chain rather than the selected lake passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Claro inlet to the central lake passage
correspondence.finding: The inlet opens into the continuous Fagnano/Khami water body. The selection turns west inside that lake; it is not an additional named river reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Long westward transboundary lake interval
correspondence.finding: The provincial basin map in the APN plan depicts continuous Fagnano across the national boundary, accounting for the long lake-scale selection. IGM independently depicts the western Chilean portion.

correspondence.component_scope: Western lake narrowing and outlet approach
correspondence.finding: IGM’s western lake polygon and the regional basin map establish the narrowing and west-northwest outlet approach. Shoreline-scale differences are not treated as a distinct channel transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Named Azopardo outlet
correspondence.finding: IGM explicitly labels the west-northwest outlet Río Azopardo. Its line follows the selected valley from the western end of Fagnano toward the head of Seno Almirantazgo.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected western terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected part reaches the Azopardo outlet/head-of-Seno-Almirantazgo setting shown by IGM linework and the provincial basin map. APN and SSRH prose identify this marine receiver. The selected tip is retained without asserting exact coincidence with the shorter source-line endpoint or a surveyed shoreline.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and initial southeastward turn across the state-border surroundings
correspondence.finding: The state original covers the chosen western opening and border-area turn. Its neighboring intermittent watercourses do not establish a continuous channel following this selected opening and turn. The Reynosa profile adds physiographic context on the eastern side, without a matching named initial stream.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastward return toward the La Llorona surroundings
correspondence.finding: The selected return is geographically near the mapped La Llorona waterbody and Plan de Ayala surroundings. Reynosa hydrography identifies La Llorona as a presa. Neither original establishes the full selected connection to, or passage through, that waterbody; the reservoir name remains adjacent context.

correspondence.component_scope: La Llorona–Doroteo Arango agricultural-plain traverse
correspondence.finding: Original mapping places the traverse across the agricultural plain and the road corridor near Doroteo Arango. It does not show a continuous watercourse accounting for the selected links across this interval. Municipal basin membership and local stream inventories cannot fill that gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward approach to the mapped waterbody at Santa Apolonia
correspondence.finding: The state original locates the selected eastward approach toward the mapped small waterbody at Santa Apolonia. The Río Bravo relief map supplies the corresponding southern waterbody setting but no continuous western feeder. This waterbody is not assigned the name Vaso La Mesa, which the municipal map places separately farther north.

correspondence.component_scope: Santa Apolonia–El Realito–El Moquetito managed corridor
correspondence.finding: The southeastern selection follows the mapped straight canal corridor beside El Realito and west of Valle Hermoso toward El Moquetito. The original legend identifies its dot-marked line as canal symbology. This supports a managed-water corridor at ordinary map scale, including the small internal joins, without an observed channel name or natural-river identity.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower departure from El Moquetito toward La Libertad Número Dos
correspondence.finding: The original depicts a canal approaching La Libertad Número Dos from the Centenario de la Constitución side and a branched lagoon-margin waterbody. The selected lower continuation departs from that depicted route. The inspected originals do not establish the selected through-link across this lower plain to the lagoon margin; this is more than an unspecified exact-bank position.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal at the Bahía Rincón de las Bayas–Laguna Madre margin
correspondence.finding: The actual tip is in the lagoon-edge setting beside La Libertad Número Dos. The state original names the adjoining bay Bahía Rincón de las Bayas, and the Matamoros relief map places this western embayment within the Laguna Madre setting. This identifies the terminal waterbody context, not an independently verified river mouth or the Gulf entrance.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening northwest of Malapai Hill
correspondence.finding: The selected opening occupies the western apron northwest of Malapai Hill. The original maps show the named Fried Liver Wash farther east, continuing south past the hill, but do not show a feeder linking the chosen initial apron to that wash. The later approach reaches the mapped wash setting; the chosen initial through-link remains unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Fried Liver Wash through Pleasant Valley
correspondence.finding: The mapped wash bends east below Malapai Hill, passes the vegetated valley patch and Pleasant Valley, and follows the canyon toward the Washington Wash receiving setting. Repeated Fried Liver Wash labels and continuous mapped channel support this selected western corridor. Washington Wash is separately labelled as an adjoining southern corridor; it is not substituted for the entire selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Western Pinto Basin fan transfer
correspondence.finding: The source distinguishes Fried Liver Wash and Washington Wash as channels extending northeast across the fan to Pinto Wash. The selected route instead turns north across intervening ground and reaches an unnamed channel approaching Pinto Wash from the west. The detailed original does not depict that selected northward cross-fan connection. The mapped channels share a receiving system, but that fact alone does not establish this chosen transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Pinto Wash and incoming desert-wash joins
correspondence.finding: Repeated Pinto Wash labels follow the eastward and northeastward selected receiving corridor. The map shows the Smoke Tree Wash approach from the south and San Bernardino Wash approach from the northwest, with their receiving junctions in the Pinto corridor. These distinct tributary labels do not rename the complete selected system.

correspondence.component_scope: Pinto Wash across the main basin and eastern bend
correspondence.finding: The original cartography follows Pinto Wash east across the broad basin floor along the north side of the Eagle Mountains and around the eastern bend. Kunkel describes the eastward sandy drainage and its southward passage between the Eagle and Coxcomb Mountains. This supplies ordinary corridor correspondence across the basin, without requiring coincidence with individual ephemeral threads.

correspondence.component_scope: Eagle-Coxcomb outlet and lower Pinto Wash fan
correspondence.finding: The selected southward passage follows the directly labelled Pinto Wash between the Eagle and Coxcomb Mountains, crosses the Colorado River Aqueduct setting and continues down the lower fan toward the plantation area. The aqueduct and nearby artificial basins are distinct mapped features; the selected route is not assigned their names or treated as an aqueduct route. The mapped wash becomes less explicit near cultivated ground, while the independent study establishes its receiving drainage toward Palen Lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower valley connection to Palen Lake
correspondence.finding: The source map places the selected lower plain and eastward approach between the lower Pinto Wash fan and Palen Lake. Kunkel expressly identifies the Pinto drainage system as discharging to Palen Lake, supporting this general receiving relationship at ordinary valley scale. A precise contemporary channel through plantations, road crossings or the final lake-margin fan is not established or required for this bounded relationship; no present operation or current inundation is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Palen Lake passage and southwest margin
correspondence.finding: Palen Lake is directly labelled on the mapped dry-lake polygon. The selected route crosses its western/southwestern lake setting and follows the southern marginal plain. This supports the lake identification and ordinary passage setting; it does not establish an outlet channel or an onward natural-river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Palen-to-Ford plain and alluvial-fan transfer
correspondence.finding: The selected extension continues southeast from the Palen Lake margin across the broad plain and fan toes west and south of the Palen Mountains toward Ford Dry Lake. The original map depicts separate playas, discontinuous drainage markings and alluvial fans, but no through-channel establishing the complete selected inter-playa transfer. The independent project figure distinguishes Palen Lake and Ship Creek-Ford Dry Lake watershed areas; watershed boundaries are not proof of the selected hydraulic connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual Ford Dry Lake terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected parts and endpoint lie in the western portion of the mapped Ford Dry Lake complex north of Interstate 10. The dry-lake label and polygon directly establish the actual terminal setting. This is distinct from Palen Lake upstream and does not close the unsupported intervening plain transfer.
